Objects: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. Define P_b(t)=integral 1_{s<min(t,T)}*b(s)d lambda_T(s) for every t in R_+.

Domains: T in R_+; b:R_+->R; no probability space or filtration.

Quantifiers: For every T and b, if b is integrable for lambda_T, then the conclusion holds.

Assumptions: b is lambda_T-integrable. No continuity, sign restriction, or strict positivity of T is assumed.

Conclusion: The scalar function P_b has bounded variation on the nonnegative interval [0,T].

Scopes: BoundedVariationOn refers only to [0,T]. The prefix body is specified for all t>=0 using a strict cutoff and clipping at T. The conclusion does not state a numerical total-variation bound or assert equality to integral |b|.

Constant dependencies: No explicit existential or uniform constant is part of the theorem statement; the finite variation bound implicit in bounded variation may depend on b,T.
